rationale: Consistency fix on the primary question. Its latest interpretation is the read-index boundary control, which carries no defect judgment, so a reader taking the latest version as the current account would see the finding restated as a boundary observation. This revision merges the complete account into one current interpretation: the witness series, the flags and clock variant, the participant-form control, the admission-on-re-arm observation and the read-index boundary, with the defect claim asserted as before and every cited receipt listed with its indices.

interpretations.rationale: Ten retained executions establish the account. Witness: with node 3 dropped from both halves and re-admitted, and no leader change observed, invocations on it do not return inside the observed windows (1201 ms, 800/801 ms, 900 ms, 2000 ms), release only at the caller's deadline, leave no committed payload, and are admitted unmodified once a leader change re-arms the gate (4637 ms after issue) with the payload then committed. This holds with a context that never expires, with retries, with the clock running, and under PreVote plus CheckQuorum, and the same holds for a configuration change proposed through the same member. Controls: a never-removed member returns in 0 ms and commits; a member kept as an outgoing voter of a joint configuration that is never left returns and commits; and a read-index request from the disarmed member completes with a read state while its proposal stays held, so the harm is confined to the MsgProp entry points. Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), 377 (no leader) and 426 (local member removed) and used as the receive case at node.go:386; the removal guard fires exactly when applying a conf change deletes the local Progress entry, which LeaveJoint does for outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set; the snapshot's own node test scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader, which is not this case. The defect is the interval itself: a member that is a voter with a healthy, known leader cannot get proposals or configuration proposals to any decision and receives no error signal, until an unrelated leader change admits them.

knowledge.assertion: propc is armed only on observed leader change and is left nil after a re-admission
the caller sends on n.propc and stays pending while the run loop's gate variable is disarmed; a later observed leader change admits the pending request
the raft state machine returns ErrProposalDropped for a removed leader instead of blocking
intended blocking is scoped to the unknown-leader case and acceptance is expected once a leader is known; re-addition is untested
a configuration change proposed through the re-added voter was held pending and was not applied by any node
a joint-consensus removal with automatic leave leads to the same held-proposal effect after the member is re-added
advancing the logical clock left the held invocation pending with leader 1 still in StateLeader
the effect persists under PreVote and CheckQuorum with the clock advanced before the invocation
on the disarmed member a read-index completion arrived while the proposal stayed held and uncommitted

counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised (propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.
No request is lost: held invocations are admitted unmodified once the gate is re-armed, so the harm is an unbounded wait without an error signal rather than data loss or a protocol safety violation.

The controls show the opposite outcome for a never-removed member, for an outgoing voter, for configuration proposals only (read index still completes), and for the same member after a leader change, so the effect is neither general nor a mere function of any configuration change.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were unknown because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose and RawNode.ProposeConfChange have no such gate. Delivery is reliable throughout, so loss and partition behaviour is not characterized.

Clock schedules executed were ten rounds with delivery between rounds, under default flags and under PreVote plus CheckQuorum; partitions in which the member hears no leader traffic were not executed.

Removal forms executed: simple ConfChange removal and joint-implicit removal with automatic leave; the participant-form control covers an outgoing voter that is never left, while incoming-voter and learner forms were not executed as controls.
The configuration-proposal case was executed once (add node 9) in one window, and the read-index boundary once; both establish the direction of the effect rather than a distribution.

The restarted-member scenario shows the opposite arrangement (a member that starts without a leader arms the gate when it learns one), so the defect is specific to re-admission while a leader is already believed known.
interpretations.joint_history: The witness series is the seven-receipt lineage on one fixed scenario (43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad, a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f, 87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4, 905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8, 6e187216178a49d4ae02bd8c2afaeaf9, bd84c33f4fe647bc9470b0b48f324bca, e7cdea5042e54182b277e185ae576ea8): configuration {1,2,3}, leader 1 at term 1, removal of node 3 by committed change, re-addition, the same invocations and a forced campaign of node 2 into term 2. Three further receipts belong to the same investigation and harness: 0bd684d77ff947f7bb85883d5dbb3dc2 is the lineage's successor with PreVote and CheckQuorum and the clock advanced; 99416a609e5242adbf53c527cc526cba comes from the child investigation's control experiment and contains that run's witness events plus the participant-form contrast; c1832eb92178495590b39614c72a880a comes from the read-index boundary experiment and contains the disarmed member's read-index completion with its held proposal. All of them share the harness, node set, removal and re-addition procedure and the witness definitions, so the cited indices belong to their own run of the same witnesses or to a deliberate contrast case.
